title: How a Rider and the Allowance Card Sit Beside the Dental, Vision and Hearing Benefits of a Ridgecrest Advantage Plan
content:
Holding an Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders rider changes how a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan pays dental, vision and hearing services: the rider's own annual maximum is applied first, and only what the rider does not cover is charged against the plan's embedded allowance for that benefit.

**Condition of record.** The rider the member holds is in force on the date of service of the line the plan is paying. The member's rider records are the authority, tested before the line is paid and matched on the member reference; a rider counts as in force where it stands active or in its waiting period.

### Never stacked

The two are never stacked into one larger payment for a single service, and the plan never pays twice for the same line.

### Where the member holds no rider

Where the member holds no rider the plan's embedded allowance applies on its own, and once that allowance is exhausted for the contract year further services of that kind are the member's own cost and do not count toward the maximum out-of-pocket.

### The allowance card and the start of coverage

Bringing the medical plan into force opens the Supplemental Benefit Allowance Programmes card programme the plan held carries and makes the first quarterly load available on the coverage effective date; the card is never opened before coverage begins. A member whose plan carries no allowance card is told so plainly rather than being enrolled in a card programme with nothing on it.

*A member holds a dental rider and has a course of dental work.* The rider's own annual maximum is applied to that work first, and only the part the rider does not cover is charged against the embedded dental allowance of the Ridgecrest Advantage plan held.
